question.text: In an experiment for estimating the value of focal length of converging mirror, image of an object placed at <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>40</mn><mo> </mo><mi>cm</mi></math> from the pole of the mirror is formed at distance <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>120</mn><mo> </mo><mi>cm</mi></math> from the pole of the mirror. These distances are measured with a modified scale in which there are <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>20</mn></math> small divisions in <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>1</mn><mo> </mo><mi>cm</mi></math>. The value of error in measurement of focal length of the mirror is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mi>K</mi></mfrac><mo> </mo><mi>cm</mi></math>. The value of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>K</mi></math> is ______.

solution.text:
Given here, u=-40 cm, v=-120 cm

Using mirror formula, 1v+1u=1f

 -1120-140=1f⇒f=-30 cm

Now, differentiating mirror equation, we get

-1v2dv-1u2du=-1f2df

Also, the least count of scale, dv=du=120 cm

Putting in above equation, 

∴ 120(120)2+120(40)2=df(30)2

On solving, we get

df=132 cm

∴ K=32.
